answers.question: What is the dot that jumps between P and Q while the stars stay still?

observations.morphology: one native pixel above 5x the frame median in its 3x3 neighbourhood in both frames

pointing.note: The same detector pixel maps to sky positions this far apart because the two pointings differ. Field-star peaks (native local maxima, quantized to ~6.2 arcsec native pixels) stay within the listed distance of their fixed Gaia positions in each frame.

answers.calculation: WCS (key A) detector coordinates of the native local maximum; WCS celestial position of the same pixel centre in P and Q; separation in arcsec.
answers.image_reference: contact_sheet.png, yellow boxes at display (114.9, 82.9) in P and (117.9, 80.6) in Q; bottom row shows the shipped flag overlay (red) covering it
answers.supported_conclusion: The jumping dot is one flagged native pixel (NONFUNC, TRANSIENT, SUR_ERROR) at the same detector pixel in P and Q. It shifts on the sky grid because the pointing differs. The flags and single-pixel morphology do not justify treating it as a moving or new source.

n2_crosscheck.fact: Detector pixel (1709,1364): sky jump 5.36 arcsec, 3.81 display px. Three strict-quality Gaia field stars agree between P and Q to median 0.40 arcsec (max 0.76); their detector shift (about -0.83, -0.28 native px) predicts 5.38 arcsec for a detector-fixed pixel. R's cutout does not contain detector pixel (1709,1364).

answers.limit: The flags say the pixel is unusable and that a transient was detected during onboard processing; they do not establish a physical cause (no cosmic-ray, hot-pixel or other mechanism is claimed). R's cutout does not contain this detector pixel, so R's background at that sky position is only a statement about the sky there, not evidence about the detector pixel.

answers.calculation: census in results.json bright_spots (native local maxima >= the frame's display high).
answers.supported_conclusion: One more flagged single pixel sits at R's edge (NONFUNC, TRANSIENT, SUR_ERROR). One unflagged, star-like spot near display (128, 31) is present in all three frames with similar values; it is a steady source not in the G < 17 Gaia cache and is not identified.

answers.question: Q looks brighter overall than P in the preset view (and C differs from A/B in the case view). Is that the sky?

stretch_probe_preset_per_frame.note: Same sky value, different displayed grey: each shipped frame has its own stretch (display_scale.mode = per_frame). Rounding to 8-bit is approximate.

stretch_probe_staged_case.note: Staged case products: P and Q on one shared stretch (ingest shared_groups_for_case), R on its own.

frame_background.note: Medians of the display-grid pixel values in the record unit (MJy / sr). Descriptive only: no background model, calibration check or uncertainty; not photometry.

answers.calculation: grey = 255 asinh(10 t)/asinh(10), t = clip((v - low)/(high - low)); low/high from each record's display_scale (or the shared P+Q limits); background = median of display-grid values.
answers.image_reference: contact_sheet.png: top row tiles 1-2 (per-frame) vs tiles 4-5 (shared P+Q stretch)
answers.supported_conclusion: The same input radiance gets a different grey level under each frame's own stretch (1.0 MJy/sr: grey 156 in P, 174 in Q), so the per-frame stretch changes grey levels between frames. Under one shared stretch the same value gets the same grey (159 in both). Q's grid median is 0.971 of P's, yet the per-frame stretch draws Q lighter; under the shared stretch the order reverses.

n2_crosscheck.fact: 1.0 MJy/sr -> grey 156 (P) / 174 (Q) per-frame, 159 / 159 shared; observed PNG grey ranges agree.
Shipped per-frame PNG median grey Q 20 vs P 16; shared stretch P 19 vs Q 16; physical median Q/P = 0.971.

answers.limit: This proves a display effect exists; it does not prove every frame-wide brightness difference has only that cause, and the small physical difference in median (Q 0.971 of P) has no established cause. The medians are descriptive, uncalibrated and carry no uncertainty; no brightness change or constancy is measured. For R (C in the case), wavelength also differs.

external_sources.label: Dore et al. 2014, SPHEREx cosmology design paper (arXiv:1412.4872)
external_sources.fact: All-sky point-source requirement of about 18.5 AB mag (5 sigma) per spectral element after the full survey; a single exposure is shallower.

answers.supported_conclusion: The marker is a catalog prediction, not an image detection. The dot nearest it lies 0.7-0.8 arcsec from the catalogued Gaia DR3 star 5756956644387831296 and 4.2-8.7 arcsec from the marker: a positional association with that star, so it is not evidence of WISE 0855.
answers.limit: A positional association is not an identification; the first moment is crude (3x3, undersampled PSF). That WISE 0855 is far below SPHEREx sensitivity at 1.26-1.44 um is a sourced expectation (published J-band brightness vs SPHEREx design depth), not a measured non-detection or an upper limit. In Q two PERSIST-flagged pixels sit inside the screen circle next to this dot.

answers.question: Can P and R show whether WISE 0855 moved?

near_marker_R.method: brightest native local maximum within 3 native px of the marker; 3x3 first moment above the frame median

answers.calculation: pairs.P-R; predicted shift from the catalog markers only.

n2_crosscheck.fact: P-Q: delta lambda 0.0018 band widths (smaller band width), same detector, release, software and rotation; differ in pipeline build, stretch, quality screen, pointing (0.87 native px). P-R: 184.8 d, 6.22 band widths, field rotated about 180 deg.

answers.supported_conclusion: P/R does not establish WISE 0855 motion here: the target is not securely detected or identified in these frames, and no astrometric fit was made. The pair also mixes 185 days with a 0.18706 um wavelength change (6.225 band widths).
answers.limit: No universal rule is implied: positions can be compared across wavelengths, and shifts below one native pixel can be measured with a detected source, adequate signal, PSF knowledge and a proper fit. Wavelength, PSF, sensitivity, sampling and quality all have to be considered; here the first requirement (a detected, identified target) already fails.
